name: Tropical rainforest
notes: Ever-wet lowland rainforest: multi-layered evergreen broadleaf forest with buttressed canopy, giant emergents, palms, lianas and heavy epiphyte load. Drawn on the Amazon, Congo Basin and Sundaland (Borneo/Malaya) dipterocarp forest.

emergent.name: Brazil nut tree
emergent.source: Bertholletia excelsa, Brazil nut, emergent of non-flooded Amazon terra firme forest, 30-50 m — Wikipedia / Kew

emergent.name: Kapok
emergent.source: Ceiba pentandra, kapok, buttressed emergent of neotropical and West African rainforest, up to 70 m — Wikipedia

emergent.name: Tualang
emergent.source: Koompassia excelsa, tualang/mengaris, tallest emergent of Sundaland lowland rainforest (Borneo, Malaya), up to 80+ m — Wikipedia

emergent.name: Yellow meranti
emergent.source: Shorea faguetiana, yellow meranti dipterocarp, Borneo lowland forest emergent, record 100 m tropical tree — Wikipedia / Nature 2019

canopy.name: Sapucaia
canopy.source: Lecythis pisonis, sapucaia (monkey-pot), Amazon/Atlantic forest canopy tree with pink flush, 20-35 m — Wikipedia / Kew

canopy.name: Limba
canopy.source: Terminalia superba, limba/afara, layered-crown canopy tree of Congo Basin and West African rainforest, 30-50 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

canopy.name: Red meranti
canopy.source: Shorea leprosula, light red meranti, dominant dipterocarp of Sundaland lowland forest canopy, 30-50 m — Wikipedia / IUCN

canopy.name: Strangler fig
canopy.source: Ficus aurea, Florida/Caribbean strangler fig; Ficus lianes typical of all tropical rainforests, 15-30 m on host trees — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Assai palm
canopy.source: Euterpe precatoria, acai palm, most abundant tree species of the Amazon (ter Steege 2013), slender palm 10-25 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Rattan palm
canopy.source: Calamus manan, manau rattan, climbing spiny palm of Malesian rainforest, stems 40+ m long — Wikipedia / PROSEA

shrub.name: Giant bamboo
shrub.source: Dendrocalamus giganteus, giant bamboo, SE Asian monsoon and rainforest margins, clumps 15-30 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Tree fern
shrub.source: Cyathea arborea, West Indian tree fern, neotropical rainforest understory and gaps, 3-9 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Heliconia
shrub.source: Heliconia bihai, red palulu/lobster claw, neotropical rainforest understory herb 1.5-4 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Silver miconia
shrub.source: Miconia argentea, Melastomataceae pioneer shrub/treelet common in neotropical rainforest understory and gaps, 2-8 m — Wikipedia / STRI

shrub.name: Aframomum ginger
shrub.source: Aframomum melegueta, grains of paradise, Zingiberaceae understory herb of West/Central African rainforest, 1-2.5 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

ground.name: Forest-floor fern
ground.source: Adiantum latifolium, maidenhair fern, common terrestrial fern of shaded neotropical rainforest floor, 0.3-0.8 m — Wikipedia / Tropicos

ground.name: Selaginella
ground.source: Selaginella willdenowii, peacock spikemoss, iridescent blue-green ground carpet of SE Asian rainforest floor — Wikipedia

ground.name: Marantaceae herb
ground.source: Calathea lutea, cigar calathea, large-leaved neotropical rainforest floor herb 1-3 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Amazon sword
ground.source: Echinodorus grandiflorus, Amazon sword plant, emergent along rainforest creek margins, 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Bromeliad
epiphyte.source: Guzmania lingulata, scarlet star bromeliad, epiphytic tank bromeliad of neotropical rainforest canopy — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Orchid
epiphyte.source: Cattleya labiata, crimson cattleya, epiphytic orchid of Brazilian rainforest canopy — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Bird's nest fern
epiphyte.source: Asplenium nidus, bird's nest fern, large epiphytic fern of Asian/Australasian rainforest trunks and branches — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Monstera
epiphyte.source: Monstera deliciosa, split-leaf philodendron, hemi-epiphytic climber of Central American rainforest, climbing 20 m — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Liana
epiphyte.source: Bauhinia guianensis, monkey-ladder liana, flattened woody climber of Amazon canopy, 40 m — Wikipedia / Tropicos
